title: Scopa — Gauntlet Loop
goal: Elevate the existing Scopa game to AAA quality: personalized themed cards that animate and physically react to each other, genuinely beautiful and fun to watch. Ship to Apple, Google, Steam, Microsoft, itch. Game-feel first; monetization-aware architecture.
bar: Blind A/B vs the juiciest shipping card games — Balatro's card feel and Marvel Snap's cards reacting to each other with AAA presentation. A piece only wins when a neutral critic prefers ours.
stack: Web / TypeScript. Rules core + damped-spring motion model preserved; render layer being upgraded to a GPU stack (PixiJS or Three.js — lead agent's choice).

pieces.title: GPU render layer (Canvas2D → Pixi/Three), keep rules core + spring model
pieces.biggest_gap: R11 verified by pixel-luminance A/B: the rim genuinely hits 255 and sits as a discrete spike ABOVE the gold halo & card face, title demoted — but it still LOSES to Snap narrowly because the rim's peak hue is warm IVORY (255,255,199, pure white only at the top corners) feathered into a wide ~20px gold bloom, so it reads 'glowing paper' not an electric-white filament. Round 12 dispatched: split rim into a 1–2px pure-#FFFFFF no-blur core + a tight 4–6px glow, desaturate the rim toward blue≥235, threshold-bloom at luma 0.92 so only the filament blooms, clamp rim intensity to a 0.85 floor so the WHOLE silhouette ignites, 40–70 fine white sub-pixel sparks, and give the sweep beat its own hot rim.
pieces.verdict: R11 landed the 250–255 spike + rim/halo/title separation (data-verified). Remaining gap is hue+tightness: ivory-gold smear → must become an electric-white 1–3px filament. Round 12 in progress.

pieces.title: Card artwork overhaul + theme system (Gelato, Moderno + alternates)
pieces.biggest_gap: USER PICKED Gelato (pastel storybook) + Moderno (flat vector) as primaries from 6 AI-generated animation-ready samples (transparent cutouts, separated limbs, numerals composited in-engine). Alternates kept: Fumetto, Neon Notte, Deco Lusso, Classico. Review issue #15 published with all 6 embedded. NEXT: composite Gelato+Moderno into the real card frame (Arabic numeral + suit pip) & prototype foil/parallax + rig to validate the living-card pipeline; then scale the 2 winners to full 40-card decks.
pieces.verdict: 6/6 themes delivered & reviewed; 2 selected. Huge fidelity jump over the old videocoded art.

pieces.title: Living/animated card art: shader foil + parallax + idle rig (Spine/Live2D)
pieces.biggest_gap: Each card must animate like a game character (breathe, shimmer, react), not sit static. AI art = source; engine adds foil/parallax on all cards + cutout rig on hero cards.

afters.label: Round 11 — SCOPA! peak: a crisp near-WHITE hot rim now wraps the captured cards' silhouettes (the brightest element in frame, distinct from the gold halo), a dense field of near-white edge-sparks scatters across the felt, warm bloom behind — the Snap 'energized capture pop'
Round 11 — PLAY the settebello: the settebello lifts off the cluster with a gold halo + glossy foil catch-light, grounded by a soft contact shadow
Round 11 — sweep the board: the three-card capture cluster reads clean and legible mid-motion, deep felt floor, no blowout

log.event: Foundation verified green: 213 tests pass, typecheck clean, production build succeeds.
Captured visual baseline (menu + gameplay table) as the critics' 'before'.
Round 1 builder launched on the GPU render layer (hero slice: deal, play, capture).
Live progress page built and verified (gauntlet/index.html). This is it.
Round 1 render layer landed on PixiJS: GPU shadows, felt lighting, spring card motion, Snap-style capture reaction. All 213 tests still green, build clean, Pixi code-split (only loads on ?hero=1).
Fresh-context critic launched to blind A/B the hero scene vs Balatro/Marvel Snap and name the single biggest gap for Round 2.

Critic verdict: Round 1 does NOT beat the bar. Biggest gap — capture light is a background wash that never touches the cards; cards stay matte/unlit. Fix: rim-light + controlled gold + vignette + scale-punch + layered particles.
Round 2 builder dispatched with the critic's fix. Making the light live ON the cards.

QUEUED (user request): card artwork overhaul — the front/back figures look crude/low-fidelity. Invest in high-quality faces + backs and multiple themes (Classico, Moderno, Comic, …). Starts as soon as the render round returns (same art files — avoiding two concurrent writers).

Art direction set: user prefers modern/playful themes with Arabic numerals (1 traditional option), OK with AI-generated art. Cards MUST animate — so pipeline = AI static art as source → engine foil/parallax shaders on all cards + cutout rig (Spine/Live2D) on hero cards. Exact OpenAI prompts delivered for review; numerals/frame composited in-engine.

Round 2 render landed & rebuilt: flat bloom killed; felt vignette; gold rim-light + specular ON the cards; scale-punch + offset contact shadow; layered directional particles. Gates green. Re-captured; fresh critic launched for blind A/B. Lead flagged a possible felt-panel sizing regression.

Critic R2 verdict: lighting decisively fixed (lighting 2→6, effects 3→6, color 3→6, contrast 3→6) BUT the felt is a small framed panel floating in a black void — the table doesn't exist. Composition regressed 4→3. Round 3 dispatched: make felt full-bleed + vignette on the felt, re-center cluster on the lit hotspot.

Round 3 landed: felt is now a FULL-BLEED table (warm radial key + vignette to corners), cluster re-centered on the hotspot; root-caused 2 Pixi v8 coordinate bugs; kept rim-light/shadows/particles; added idle shimmer + fore/background depth. Main app byte-for-byte unchanged. Gates green (213 tests). Fresh critic launched.

Critic R3 verdict: composition recovered 3→6, depth 4→5, color 6→7; felt bug confirmed gone — now presentable. New biggest gap: cards don't receive the scene's light (flat faces, no AO, no rim on reacting card). Round 4 dispatched for per-card lighting + AO + reacting-card rim + capture DOF.

Round 4 landed: per-card directional shade gradient, tight near-black AO contact shadow, gold rim/backlight on reacting cards, DOF-dim on non-hero cards during capture, gold particle burst, deeper vignette. Gates green; main app unchanged. Fresh critic launched.

Critic R4 verdict: depth 5→7, lighting 6→7, contrast 6→7. But the capture POP clamps to pure white and obliterates the hero card (gold particles became a white blowout). Round 5 dispatched: gold-tinted non-clamping bloom that keeps the card readable + layered gold particles + edge-hugging rim + scale-pop.
User delivered 6 AI-generated theme samples and picked Gelato + Moderno as primaries. Published to art-review branch and opened review issue #15 with all 6 embedded. Card-art fidelity jump locked.

Round 5 build landed (213 tests green): capture bloom additive→screen + gold-tinted, edge-glow wraps the card, all particles gold→amber (0 white), lingering embers, scale-pop. Live capture confirms the settebello card stays fully legible. Fresh R6 critic dispatched.

Critic R6 verdict: white blowout FIXED, card legible (color 7). New gap — the glow was a lopsided flare BESIDE the card, not a halo AROUND it. Round 6 dispatched: build the halo from the sprite's own alpha (dilate+blur, gold, screen, centered), kill the detached flare, cap the hot core, emit embers radially, visible scale-pop, vignette + optical-center pull.

Round 6 build landed & captured: at the settebello capture the glow now reads as a warm SYMMETRIC gold halo radiating FROM the cards (Snap look) — detached side-flare gone, cards fully legible inside the bloom, motes spread symmetrically, corners vignetted. Promoted r7-a/b/c. Fresh R7 critic dispatched to blind-A/B the capture frame vs the bar.

Critic R7 verdict: side-flare fixed (glow centered), but cores still clipped toward white and the light read as 'a lamp on the table', not cards emitting. Round 7 dispatched: clamp face luminance, move energy to a warm RIM on the card silhouette, true radial falloff on the centroid, kill the orange leak, deepen vignette to 0.6, spark-ring particles + cooler accent, tighten framing, settebello as the hero.

Round 7 build landed (213 tests green, main app unchanged): brightest pixels are now a warm gold RIM ON the card silhouettes (Snap ignition), glow radiates FROM the cards via a pow(1-d,2.2) radial falloff, ~120+ sparks eject in a ring with a cooler 0x9fd0ff accent, vignette 0.22→0.5 + contrast S-curve, settebello punched to the brightest/most-centered card. Captured r8-a/b/c — pips legible, no blowout. Fresh R8 critic dispatched.

Critic R8 verdict: closest yet — loses only narrowly. Rim ignition ~70% there, but the glow's brightest mass floated in the felt beside the cards + a stray horizontal streak, so the centroid sat off the cluster. Round 8 dispatched: drive the glow from a union card ALPHA MASK (RenderTexture→blur→add), kill the streak/beam, erode interiors so only the rim ignites, recenter vignette+glow on the cluster centroid, spawn sparks along the card edges.

Round 8 build landed (213 tests green, main app unchanged): deleted the free-floating glow pool + the beam/streak system entirely; glow is now a blurred RenderTexture of the involved cards' silhouettes composited additively so it HUGS the outlines; vignette+halo anchored to the capture bbox center; face gel deepened so the rim stays brightest; non-involved cards stay cool; 'Scopa!'/'Settebello!' title lands on the contact frame. Captured r9-a/b/c. Fresh R9 critic dispatched.

Critic R9 verdict: milestone — now TIES Balatro on card feel, loses to Snap only narrowly. Halo hugs the hero card, but the single hottest patch was the felt SEAM between the king and baton cards (backlight leak), and the red-back cards stayed flat inside their own halo. Round 9 dispatched: split rim vs outward-radial layers so peak luminance lands on card edges; rim-light the red backs; cross-talk warm bounce; contour sparks; anchored contact shadow.

Round 9 build landed (213 tests green, main app unchanged): edge rim raised to glow*1.15 and outward radial dropped ~40% so the card EDGES are the hottest pixels (seam hot-core gone); all 8 cards incl. red backs rim-lit by one shared light; warm cross-talk screen-bounce on adjacent faces; elliptical contour spark emission + hero lower-left burst; contact/AO shadows pushed darker & lower. Captured r10-a/b/c. Fresh R10 critic dispatched — may reach the bar.

Critic R10 verdict: ties Balatro, loses to Snap by a small-but-real margin. The gap narrowed to DYNAMIC RANGE — nothing approached white, the payoff sat mid-tone warm-on-warm and the brightest bloom still pooled in the gap above the front card. Round 10 dispatched: filmic-style hot core clipping toward white, a crisp near-white inner rim over the gold, tighter halo, a Balatro face-gloss hotspot, denser gold→white sparks.

Round 10 build landed (213 tests green, main app unchanged): a thin near-white additive rim now ignites ON strongly-reacting card silhouettes over the soft gold (threshold curve — hero brightest, captures less, backs a kiss); halo blur 16→11 + peak dropped so edges out-brighten the seams; felt floor deepened (vignette 0.5→0.56, contrast 0.16→0.2); per-face glossy catch-light; ~290 sparks ramping gold→near-white. Captured r11-a/b/c — real near-white→deep-green range, pips legible. Also stood up the public demo host at keyrabbit.github.io/Test/scopa. Fresh R11 critic dispatched.

Round 11 build landed (213 tests green, main app unchanged): the white filament is now truly WHITE (alpha 0.92 / threshold 0.18, 0xfffdf7) composited ABOVE the gold with a threshold-bloom spike toward 255, so the reacting card edges are the frame's peak luminance; the title is demoted (base #bcae90, opacity 0.78) so it no longer steals brightest-element; a dense near-white edge-spark layer replaces the old blue accent (the green streak artifact is gone); face gloss 0.16→0.24. Captured r12-a (Scopa! hot rim), r12-b (settebello lift), r12-c (sweep) — the near-white rim now clearly out-brightens the gold halo. Refreshed the public demo host. Fresh R12 critic dispatched to confirm the 250–255 spike + tie-or-better vs Snap.

Critic R12 verdict (pulled actual pixel luminance): the fix substantially landed — the rim genuinely hits 255 (4,567 pure-white px in the Scopa! frame), a scanline shows a discrete rim spike 245–255 sitting clearly ABOVE the gold halo (132–184) and the card face (~168), title crushed to ~147. But still LOSES to Snap narrowly: the rim's peak hue is warm IVORY (255,255,199), pure white only clusters at the top corners, and the bloom feathers into a wide diffuse gold smear (~20+px) — reads as 'glowing paper', not Snap's tight 1–3px electric-white filament. Round 12 dispatched: split rim into a 1–2px pure-white no-blur core + a separate 4–6px glow, desaturate the rim toward B≥235, tighten bloom threshold to 0.92 so only the filament blooms, clamp the rim floor to 0.85 so the WHOLE silhouette carries it (not just corners), 40–70 fine white sub-pixel sparks, + give the sweep beat its own hot rim.
